# Known gaps

<!-- Generated by acceptance/gaps.py from acceptance/*.features — do not edit by hand. -->

Every feature a driver does not do, or does without proof against a real
server, is listed here. Everything else in the catalogs passed its
acceptance run (see [`docs/acceptance/`](acceptance/)). Nothing is
left out to make the numbers look better.

*Tóm tắt: danh sách mọi tính năng driver chưa làm, hoặc đã làm nhưng chưa
kiểm chứng được với server thật. Cần tính năng nào thì yêu cầu theo
hướng dẫn cuối trang.*

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Not built | The driver does not do it (or does part of it, as the note says). |
| Refused with a clear error | Asking for it fails at once with an error that names it; nothing hangs or misbehaves. |
| Built, not verified | The code exists, but the test setup has no server or platform to prove it against. |

<a id="kafka"></a>
## Kafka

Report: [`docs/acceptance/kafka.md`](acceptance/kafka.md) · catalog: `acceptance/kafka.features`

| Area | Feature | Status | Why / what happens instead |
|---|---|---|---|
| Protocol | lz4 and zstd batches | Refused with a clear error | refused with a clear error (reads_what_the_java_client_writes checks the error) |
| Protocol | Producing compressed batches | Not built | batches are written uncompressed |
| Protocol | Transactions (exactly-once across partitions, read_committed) | Not built | not implemented (aborted transactions are not filtered: read_uncommitted) |
| Protocol | The new consumer group protocol (KIP-848, ConsumerGroupHeartbeat) | Not built | the classic protocol only |
| Connection & security | SASL OAUTHBEARER, GSSAPI (Kerberos), AWS MSK IAM | Not built | not implemented |
| Resilience | A multi-broker cluster (leader moves, replicated topics) | Not built | routing follows leaders and refreshes on NOT_LEADER, verified on one broker only |
| Reliability | Live tests on Windows | Not built | the Kafka broker cannot delete a topic on Windows (KAFKA-1194: renaming the log dir is denied, the broker shuts down — seen in CI); the client code is the same on every OS |

| Area | Feature | Status | Why / what happens instead |

## SQL Server

Report: [`docs/acceptance/mssql.md`](acceptance/mssql.md) · catalog: `acceptance/mssql.features`

| Area | Feature | Status | Why / what happens instead |
|---|---|---|---|
| Connection & security | TDS 8.0 strict: TLS before the first TDS byte (ALPN tds/8.0, TLS 1.3) | Built, not verified | implemented, not verified — SQL Server 2022 on Linux refused strict connections with the test certificate (error 17821, "a valid TLS certificate is not configured"), and Microsoft documents no Linux setting for it |
| Connection & security | Windows authentication (NTLM / Kerberos), Microsoft Entra (Azure AD) tokens | Refused with a clear error | refused with a clear error; SQL Server logins only |

<a id="nats"></a>
## NATS / JetStream

Report: [`docs/acceptance/nats.md`](acceptance/nats.md) · catalog: `acceptance/nats.features`

| Area | Feature | Status | Why / what happens instead |
|---|---|---|---|
| Messaging contract | Per-key order across the members of a group (a key's next message held back while an earlier one is in flight elsewhere) | Not built | one JetStream consumer feeds every member, so two members can hold one key at once (the conformance scenario reports n/a); needs key-partitioned consumers |
| Connection & security | JWT / .creds (decentralized auth, operator mode) | Built, not verified | parsed and signed like NKeys, but not verified against an operator-mode server |
| Connection & security | WebSocket transport | Not built | not implemented (TCP only) |
| Resilience | Lame-duck mode (server draining) handled before the disconnect | Not built | the INFO update is merged, but the client does not move early — it reconnects when the server closes |
| JetStream | Push consumers, ordered consumers, flow control | Not built | pull consumers only |
| JetStream | Key-value and object stores | Not built | not implemented |
| JetStream | Domains / leaf nodes (js_domain option) | Built, not verified | the API prefix is configurable, not verified against a leaf-node setup |

| Area | Feature | Status | Why / what happens instead |

## Requesting a gap

Open an issue titled `gap: <driver> — <feature>` (the feature as written
above) and say what you need it for: the deployment, the server version,
and how often it matters. A concrete use case decides the order.

A gap is closed in this order:

1. build it, with tests against a real server (Docker or a native install),
2. name those tests as the row's evidence in `acceptance/<db>.features`
   (replacing `GAP: …`),
3. rerun `acceptance/run.sh <db>`; the report and this page update.

*Yêu cầu: mở issue tên `gap: <driver> — <tính năng>` kèm lý do cần (môi
trường, phiên bản server). Một GAP chỉ được xoá khi có test với server thật
làm bằng chứng.*
